talk_track: I spend my time helping independent school boards answer the technology-risk questions their outsourced IT vendors can't -- most recently AI policy and vendor accountability. Orangewood's open Instructional Technology Specialist posting assigns that hire to "Support school policies regarding AI use in student work" and to "Research, evaluate, and recommend new educational apps, software, and digital resources." The same posting asks for a Florida Educator Certificate, three years of classroom teaching, and coaching the eSports team. Here is the read worth having: AI policy and software vetting are two board-reportable risk functions, and they now sit inside a pedagogical coaching role that answers to curriculum rather than to your board. That is how a school accumulates tools nobody formally approved and has no one who can answer the trustee asking what happens when one of those vendors is breached. Who signs off today when a new app touches student data?
